name: Device intelligence / device-graph velocity features
parent_research_topic: Beava use cases — current and potential applications of beava as a real-time feature server

domain_fit.domain_name: Device intelligence / device-graph velocity features (per-fingerprint and per-(fingerprint, asset) aggregations powering device-intel vendors)
domain_fit.one_line_definition: A device-intelligence vendor (Castle, Fingerprint, TrustDecision, Incognia, Sardine, Persona, Sumsub, Forter Device, IPQS, Sift Device) decides in <50 ms on every identify / login / signup / checkout event whether the requesting device fingerprint is a trusted long-tail visitor, a multi-account abuser, a device farm node, or a recovered/synced device, using per-fingerprint and per-(fingerprint, asset) velocity, n_unique, geography-spread and proximity features computed continuously on top of a streaming fingerprint feed.
domain_fit.representative_jobs_to_be_done: 1) Compute Fingerprint-style 'Velocity Signals' (events per VisitorID, distinct IPs per VisitorID, distinct countries per VisitorID, distinct LinkedIDs per VisitorID, events per IP) over rolling 5 min / 1 h / 24 h windows for every identification call. 2) Detect device-farm / multi-accounting: 'n_unique(account_id) over fingerprint > N in 24h', 'n_unique(fingerprint) over account_id > N in 24h', 'proximity cluster of fingerprints reused across many accounts'. 3) Score per-(fingerprint, asset) cross-asset reuse: same device used across many merchant tenants, many API keys, many SKUs / listings, many wallets, many phone numbers — the canonical mule/synthetic-identity signal. 4) Power impossible-travel and geographic-spread features per fingerprint (n_unique(country), great-circle distance to last known geo, dwell-time distribution). 5) Feed downstream ML (XGBoost / LightGBM / GNN) and rules engines with consistent rolling features so customers do not re-implement velocity logic on top of the vendor's identify response.
domain_fit.event_shapes: Vendor-internal wire events emitted by mobile/web/server SDKs and pushed into beava: identify {ts, visitor_id, linked_id, ip, country, asn, ua, ja4, tenant_id, request_id}, login_attempt {ts, visitor_id, account_id_hash, tenant_id, ip, country, success}, signup_attempt {ts, visitor_id, account_id_hash, email_domain, tenant_id, ip, country, asset}, checkout {ts, visitor_id, account_id_hash, tenant_id, payment_method_hash, amount_bucket}, asset_use {ts, visitor_id, asset_type, asset_id_hash, tenant_id} where asset_type ∈ {phone, email, card_bin, wallet, listing_id, sku, api_key, coupon_id, referral_code}. Key dimensions: VisitorID (device fingerprint), LinkedID (vendor-supplied account/session id), IP, ASN, country, JA4, tenant_id (the device-intel vendor's customer), (visitor_id × asset_id_hash) composite key, (visitor_id × tenant_id) for cross-tenant device reuse.
domain_fit.feature_shapes: Heavy use of beava counters + n_unique + velocity + distance + distribution primitives over sliding 5 min / 1 h / 24 h / 7 d / 30 d windows. Per-VisitorID: count(events), n_unique(ip), n_unique(country), n_unique(linked_id), n_unique(account_id_hash), n_unique(tenant_id) (cross-customer reuse), velocity(events), distribution(country), max_distance(geo to last_geo). Per-LinkedID (account): n_unique(visitor_id), n_unique(ip), velocity(login_attempt). Per-IP: count(identify), n_unique(visitor_id). Per-(visitor_id × asset_id_hash): count(uses), velocity, age_first_seen — the cross-asset reuse signal. Per-(visitor_id × tenant_id): the cross-tenant signal. Distance primitive expresses impossible-travel; distribution primitive expresses 'country mix' and 'hour-of-day mix' fingerprint behavioral features.
domain_fit.entity_grain: Composite, dominated by VisitorID (device fingerprint) but always multi-keyed. Primary keys: visitor_id (device fingerprint, 64–128-bit), linked_id (vendor-supplied account/session), ip (v4/v6), account_id_hash, tenant_id (the device-intel vendor's customer), and ordered pairs (visitor_id × tenant_id), (visitor_id × account_id_hash), (visitor_id × asset_id_hash), (visitor_id × ip), (visitor_id × country).
domain_fit.window_semantics_required: Sliding windows dominate (5 min, 1 h, 24 h matching Fingerprint's published Velocity Signals API; longer 7 d / 30 d rolling windows for 'reputation' features). Approximate aggregates (HLL for n_unique, CMS for top-k) are acceptable on the IP / account / tenant axes because the device-intel vendor exposes the count to the downstream customer who tolerates a small relative error in exchange for unbounded cardinality. Fingerprint already documents that for visitors generating >10k distinct values in 24h, it caps at 10k and drops the 5 min / 1 h intervals — i.e., bounded-memory truncation is industry-acceptable behaviour. Tumbling windows useful only for vendor billing / reporting.
domain_fit.exactly_once_or_idempotency_needs: At-least-once is acceptable — these are risk features feeding a probabilistic score, not money. Each identify request has a stable request_id which can drive client-side dedup if the vendor wants exact counts; beava's at-least-once model is otherwise fine. Idempotency matters only for the billing meter the vendor charges its own customers on, which is a separate accounting stream.

technical_fit.latency_budget: Read p99 <10 ms is the operational target — the device-intel vendor returns velocity signals inside the identify response (Fingerprint exposes them on the Server API events endpoint and via webhook), and the end customer's auth gate / checkout flow has a 50–100 ms ceiling end-to-end. beava's sub-ms TCP+msgpack batch_get fits inside this budget with room for the vendor's own scoring step.
technical_fit.feature_freshness_sla: Sub-second to single-digit seconds. The whole value proposition of velocity signals is that the count of 'distinct IPs per visitor in the last 5 minutes' must already include the event that just landed; a 30 s lag breaks the rapid-burst detection that catches credential-stuffing and device-farm attacks. beava's push-on-event, no-broker-hop architecture matches this exactly.
technical_fit.throughput_profile: High and growing. Fingerprint publicly reports >1B device identifications per month (~385 EPS average) and 65% ARR growth on a 2.3B+ ID base; on big retail events that easily peaks 10–50x. Incognia, Castle, Sumsub, TrustDecision, Sardine and Forter run comparable order-of-magnitude volumes once enterprise pipelines (e.g., for a top-3 marketplace or top-3 fintech) are aggregated per vendor. A single beava node at ~684k EPS comfortably covers one device-intel vendor's regional shard or one big-customer slice; the global aggregate per vendor would need horizontal sharding (which beava v0 does not provide in-process). [uncertain]
technical_fit.read_to_write_ratio: Roughly 1:1 to 2:1 reads-per-write. Every identify event is one write (or N writes across multiple composite keys) plus one batched read of 20–100 velocity features that the vendor returns to its customer. Read amplification is real because each identify needs the full Velocity Signals payload across {visitor_id, linked_id, ip} × {5 min, 1 h, 24 h}, which beava's batch_get on composite keys is well-shaped for.
technical_fit.state_size_estimate: Dominated by VisitorID and (VisitorID × asset) cardinality. Fingerprint's 2.3B-identification dataset and Incognia's billions-of-devices SDK base imply a hot set in the ~10^8–10^9 fingerprint range per vendor globally, of which the 30 d active subset is typically a few × 10^8. At ~250–400 B per fingerprint feature vector (a handful of HLLs + counters + last-seen geo + distribution sketches), that is ~25–400 GB hot state per vendor — does NOT fit on a single beava box. A regional / per-tenant / per-(visitor-id prefix) shard is mandatory. Per-(visitor × asset) state is even larger if naive; HLL-only counters keep it bounded. [uncertain]
technical_fit.cardinality_pattern: Explosive on VisitorID (~10^9 globally per Fingerprint-scale vendor, ~10^8 monthly-active). Explosive on (VisitorID × asset_id_hash). Explosive on IP (residential proxy pools). Slowly-growing on tenant_id (the vendor's own customers). Bounded on country, ASN top-N, JA4. This is the most aggressive cardinality profile of any of the beava use cases reviewed — it is the canonical reason device-intelligence vendors build dedicated in-house feature backends rather than buying Tecton/Feast/Hopsworks.
technical_fit.typical_state_lifecycle_and_ttl: Fingerprint Pro documents linkedId retention at 30 or 90+ days depending on plan; the active velocity windows are 5 min / 1 h / 24 h with longer 7 d / 30 d rolling features for reputation. GDPR Recital 47 + EDPB 2/2023 push vendors toward differential retention (fraud-linked fingerprints persist longer, clean fingerprints expire faster), so per-key TTL with sliding-window eviction is structurally required. Most state is evictable within 30–90 days for non-fraud-flagged fingerprints.
technical_fit.typical_feature_count_per_decision: 30–150+ features per identify response (Fingerprint Smart Signals + Velocity Signals together expose dozens of signals already; a vendor layering its own custom velocities on top routinely produces 50–100). batch_get over a composite key set is the dominant access pattern — exactly the path beava optimises.
technical_fit.durability_requirements: Best-effort to crash-safe. These are derived risk features, not money or ledger state. Losing a 5-minute sliding window on crash degrades the vendor's risk model for a few minutes; the source-of-truth event log lives upstream in the vendor's Kafka / Kinesis. beava's WAL + snapshot is enough; many vendors would run it with WAL disabled on read-replica shards for throughput. SOC2 / ISO 27001 audit constraints on the vendor are about access control and PII handling, not on the velocity-feature store specifically.
technical_fit.deployment_topology_fit: Regional cluster / multi-region active-active is the natural shape — device-intel vendors run global SDK ingestion and serve identify responses from the nearest region (Fingerprint publishes US / EU / APAC data residency). beava v0 ships single-binary with no in-process sharding and no replication; this is the single largest architectural gap for this domain. beava could fit as a per-region shard inside the vendor's existing routing layer, but a Fingerprint-scale vendor would need to operate dozens of beava nodes hand-sharded by visitor_id prefix — workable but not a drop-in replacement for a Redis Enterprise / Aerospike cluster.

commercial_fit.who_buys: Platform / infra / ML engineering teams INSIDE the device-intelligence vendors themselves — i.e., the team at Fingerprint, Castle, TrustDecision, Incognia, Sardine, Persona, Sumsub, Forter Device, IPQS, Sift Device, SEON, ThreatMetrix, Group-IB, ThreatFabric, BureauID. NOT the end fraud team at a bank or marketplace (they are the vendor's customers). The buyer is the vendor's 'real-time features' / 'platform' team that today owns a custom Rust/Go service on top of Redis + RocksDB or Aerospike + Kafka feeding velocity signals into the identify API.
commercial_fit.market_size_signal: Device-intelligence segment is one of the fastest-growing sub-markets in fraud prevention. Fingerprint reports 65% ARR growth, >1B device identifications/month, 2.3B+ identifications dataset; the company was named fastest-growing Chicago-based company in the 2025 Deloitte Technology Fast 500 (2306% growth). Incognia tripled YoY revenue and moved to #2 global mobile-fraud-prevention provider. Sardine ('Fraud & Compliance Feature Store', 4,800 features) and Castle (Cloudflare integration May 2025) are both raising and scaling. Public pricing examples: Fingerprint Pro Plus / Enterprise custom-priced over 9M annual API calls; Sumsub $1.35–1.85 per verification with $149–299/mo floors; Persona starts $250/mo annual. Aggregate device-fingerprinting market sized at multiple hundreds of millions USD in 2025 and projected to grow at 18–25% CAGR through 2030. [uncertain]
commercial_fit.urgency_drivers: 1) AI-driven device farms and 'agentic' fraud (Sardine's 2026 'Agentic Attacks' analysis) are forcing vendors to ship new velocity primitives every quarter rather than every year. 2) Google's Feb 2025 reversal on device fingerprinting + EDPB 2/2023 + ICO pushback is driving vendors to differentiate on 'velocity + behavior' rather than just 'identification', which means the feature backend becomes the product. 3) Sumsub's finding that 76% of fraud happens post-KYC pushes vendors to bolt continuous device-velocity monitoring on top of one-shot identification (Sumsub × Fingerprint partnership Jun 2025 is the public example). 4) Multi-accounting / referral abuse / synthetic identity at marketplaces and crypto exchanges is exploding (Fingerprint's Dec 2025 Proximity Detection launch is the explicit response). 5) Cross-tenant fraud sharing pressure — device-intel vendors competing on 'network effect' want to expose 'this fingerprint is on N of your peers' platforms' which requires per-(visitor × tenant) counters at scale.
commercial_fit.regulatory_or_audit_constraints: GDPR / CCPA — device fingerprints are personal data; Recital 47 grants 'legitimate interest' for fraud prevention but requires data minimization and differential retention. ePrivacy Directive Art 5(3) and EDPB Guidelines 2/2023 (final Oct 2024) treat fingerprinting equivalently to cookies for consent purposes outside the fraud-prevention carve-out. ICO Jan 2025 guidance pushing back on Google. PSD3 / PSR (EU, applies ~mid-2026) requires PSPs to do continuous device-based velocity for login / mandate / beneficiary management. DORA (in force Jan 17 2025) operational resilience requirements on EU financial customers. SOC 2 and ISO 27001 are baseline for any vendor selling B2B — implies TLS, auth, access logs, hashing of PII at rest, all of which beava v0 lacks.
commercial_fit.time_to_value_signal: Fast for a prototype, slow for production. 2–5 days for a working 'Fingerprint Velocity Signals clone' demo on a laptop: @bv.event identify, @bv.table on visitor_id with count, n_unique(ip), n_unique(country), n_unique(linked_id), velocity primitives over 5m/1h/24h sliding windows; thin HTTP shim to mirror the Fingerprint /events response shape. 4–12 weeks for an internal pilot at a device-intel vendor once TLS, mTLS or token auth, per-tenant namespaces, and a sharding plan are added. Beyond that, replacing a production Redis Enterprise / Aerospike cluster is a 6–12 month migration regardless of the replacement.

competition.incumbents: Generic real-time stack used inside device-intel vendors today: Redis (counters + Lua + Bloom/CMS/Top-K via Redis Stack) is the overwhelming default and is documented as Fingerprint-shaped feature backends in Redis's own blog ('Digital Identity Validation with Redis: Real-Time Device Fingerprinting'); Aerospike at very high cardinality (used by ad-tech and large fraud vendors); custom in-Rust / in-Go services on RocksDB / Sled / FoundationDB; Flink / Materialize / RisingWave for SQL-on-stream pipelines feeding offline analytics; Tecton / Hopsworks / Chalk / Fennel as managed online feature stores feeding ML scorers (less common inside device-intel vendors because they want full control of the hot path).
competition.competitive_incumbent_per_domain: The buyers themselves ARE the domain incumbents — Fingerprint (Smart Signals + Velocity Signals + Proximity Detection, >1B IDs/mo), Castle (behavioral integrity, Cloudflare integration May 2025), TrustDecision (150+ data points + device fingerprint), Incognia (mobile device + location intelligence, #2 global mobile fraud), Sardine (Device + Behavior Biometrics SDK + 4,800-feature fraud feature store), Persona (KYC + device signals), Sumsub (Device Intelligence powered by Fingerprint Pro, Jun 2025 partnership), Forter Device, IPQS (300+ data points, 1B+ daily threat events), Sift Device, SEON (multi-accounting prevention via device fingerprinting), ThreatMetrix (LexisNexis), Group-IB, ThreatFabric. beava is not competing with these as a product — it would be a component inside them, competing against Redis / Aerospike / in-house Rust.
competition.beava_differentiator: 1) 50+ aggregation primitives natively cover n_unique / velocity / distribution / distance / counter — the exact shape a Fingerprint Velocity Signals re-implementation needs, with no Lua scripts. 2) Composite-key first-class: @bv.table(key=(visitor_id, asset_id_hash)) is the natural expression of 'cross-asset reuse', which on Redis is hand-rolled with key encoding tricks. 3) Sub-ms TCP+msgpack batch_get matches the inline identify-response budget tighter than Redis-Cluster + Lua. 4) Apache-2.0, no open-core, no managed-cloud requirement — attractive to device-intel vendors who refuse to depend on a Redis-Enterprise-style commercial layer because they themselves are a commercial vendor. 5) Single-binary, in-memory only, push-on-event model maps to the vendor's existing per-region SDK ingestion topology without a Kafka hop. 6) Rust core means GC-free p99, which the vendor's identify SLA depends on.
competition.where_beava_loses_today: 1) No in-process sharding and no replication — a Fingerprint-scale 10^8–10^9 visitor_id keyspace cannot live on one box, so the vendor must hand-shard externally; Redis Cluster / Aerospike / FoundationDB ship this. This is the single biggest blocker. 2) No TLS, no auth on :8081 / :8090 — disqualifying for any production deployment by a SOC2 / ISO27001 vendor without an in-VPC mTLS proxy in front. 3) No multi-tenancy primitives — a device-intel vendor with hundreds to thousands of customer tenants needs per-tenant namespaces, quotas, isolation, and per-tenant rate-limit accounting that beava v0 does not ship. 4) No triggers / 'fire when threshold crosses' — device farm and proximity alerts are event-driven and want async fan-out, not polling. 5) No secondary indexes / no 'top-k visitor_ids by 24h event count' — limits the SOC / analyst surface inside the vendor. 6) Refuse-on-network-FS + in-memory-only means the vendor has to plan local NVMe WAL and cold-start replay time; a node restart on tens of GB of hot state risks an outage during an attack. 7) No public benchmark at 10^8+ keys — the published ~684k EPS is on a single M4 core at unclear state size; cardinality-driven memory and GC-free p99 at production-scale visitor_id counts is unproven.
competition.integration_surface: Producers: the device-intel vendor's mobile / web / server SDKs already emit identify events through a CDN-fronted ingestion API (e.g., Fingerprint Pro endpoint); beava would sit behind that ingestion layer rather than facing the SDK directly. Push patterns: HTTP/JSON :8080 from the ingestion service, TCP+msgpack :8081 from a Rust ingestion shim, mobile SDK direct push is NOT realistic (SDKs hit the vendor's HTTPS endpoint, not beava). Kafka / Kinesis upstream from the ingestion service is universal at the scale of these vendors; beava's no-broker model is a deliberate choice to skip that hop for the hot velocity-feature path while the slow path (warehouse, analytics, ML training) still goes through Kafka. Consumers: the vendor's identify response builder (reads via batch_get and inlines Velocity-Signals-shaped payload), rules engines (custom DSL or Drools / FEEL), ML scorers (XGBoost / LightGBM / GNN models served from a separate process pulling features via batch_get).
competition.scoring_engine_coupling: Both, with strong separation. Inside a device-intel vendor, beava would be the pure feature backend; a rules engine (vendor-specific DSL, often customer-configurable like Castle policies) and one or more ML scorers (XGBoost, LightGBM, GNN for device-graph clustering) consume the same features via batch_get. Sardine explicitly publishes this 'feature store feeds rules engine + ML engine' shape. beava as a pure feature backend stays decoupled from both.

adoption_signals.existing_public_users_or_case_studies: No public users of beava in this domain yet. [uncertain] Comparable production systems and public references: Fingerprint Velocity Signals (5 min / 1 h / 24 h, per visitor / linkedID / IP — the canonical public spec beava would be re-implementing); Fingerprint Proximity Detection (Dec 2025 launch targeting device farms); Incognia Trusted Device Intelligence; Castle Device API and Risk Signals; Sumsub × Fingerprint Pro partnership (Jun 2025); Sardine Device & Behavior SDK + 4,800-feature feature store; TrustDecision 150+ data point device fingerprint; IPQS Device Tracker (1B+ daily events); SEON Block Multi-Accounting with Device Intelligence; Redis Enterprise public case study 'Digital Identity Validation with Redis: Real-Time Device Fingerprinting' (the most direct public architectural analog).
adoption_signals.community_discussions: No beava-specific Discord / GitHub Discussion threads located on device-intel velocity features as of the snapshot reviewed. [uncertain] Broader community: Fingerprint blog series on Velocity Signals + Proximity Detection; Castle's 'Roll your own bot detection' and 9-device-fingerprinting-solutions posts; Sardine's 'Fraud & Compliance Feature Store' blog; PayPal's billion-edges-per-day graph fraud detection write-ups; SEON / TrustDecision / Incognia engineering blogs; Hacker News threads on Castle × Cloudflare (May 2025); academic papers on device-fingerprinting SDKs (arXiv 2506.22639).
adoption_signals.examples_or_demos_in_repo: Generic fraud demo present at /tmp/docker-desktop-root/run/desktop/mnt/host/d/Code/Beava/beava/python/beava/demos/fraud (events.jsonl + schema.json). No dedicated device-intelligence / velocity-signals / multi-accounting demo identified in the repository as of the snapshot reviewed. A 1-day-build candidate demo: @bv.event identify + @bv.table on visitor_id implementing distinctIp_5m / distinctIp_1h / distinctIp_24h / distinctCountry_24h / distinctLinkedId_24h to mirror the Fingerprint Velocity Signals public schema, plus a per-(visitor_id × asset_id_hash) cross-asset reuse counter. [uncertain]
adoption_signals.adversarial_pressure_level: Maximum. This is the inner loop of an actively-adversarial market. Fingerprint, Castle, Incognia, Sumsub etc retool monthly against device-farm operators, anti-detect browsers (Multilogin, Octo Browser), GPS spoofers, emulator clouds, residential-proxy pools, and AI-driven 'agentic' attacks (Sardine 2026). Feature drift is fast and continuous, which favors a developer-ergonomic feature backend (beava's @bv.event / @bv.table primitives) over a SQL-on-Flink pipeline.

risk_and_non_goals.non_goals: 1) Long historical lookback / batch backfill of fingerprint history — beava is in-memory only, not the place to keep 12-month visitor_id history for ML training (that belongs in Parquet / a lakehouse alongside the vendor's Kafka archive). 2) The device-graph ITSELF — clustering 'all account_ids sharing a fingerprint cluster' is a graph-DB / GNN problem (TigerGraph, Memgraph, Kumo, in-house PyTorch Geometric); beava holds the velocity edges but not the multi-hop traversal. 3) The fingerprinting algorithm itself — beava is downstream of the SDK that produces visitor_id; it does not compute the fingerprint hash. 4) The identification network / device-reputation database that Fingerprint and Incognia have spent years building — beava cannot replicate that data asset, only host velocity features on top of it. 5) Acting as the vendor's customer-facing rules engine or scoring engine — beava is the feature backend; the vendor's product layer stays on top. 6) Replacing the vendor's Kafka / Kinesis archive — beava's WAL is for crash recovery of in-memory state, not for analyst-driven replay or model retraining.
risk_and_non_goals.open_engineering_gaps: Concrete features beava would need to ship to be production-grade inside a device-intel vendor, roughly in priority order: 1) In-process or sidecar sharding by visitor_id prefix with a documented rebalancing story — a 10^8–10^9 fingerprint keyspace cannot live on one box and the vendor will not hand-roll this externally for a v1 evaluation. 2) Replication / read replicas for HA — these vendors are SLA-bound to their own customers and a single-box failure cannot take the identify response path down. 3) TLS termination and mTLS or token auth on :8081 / :8090, with audit logging — disqualifying for any SOC2 / ISO27001 vendor today; trivial to add but blocking. 4) Per-tenant namespaces with quotas, isolation, and per-tenant rate-limit accounting — the vendor serves hundreds to thousands of B2B tenants and needs to bill / throttle per tenant. 5) First-class HLL / Bloom / CMS / Top-K approximate primitives and documented memory budgets per primitive — visitor_id and (visitor_id × asset) blowup requires bounded RAM and the Fingerprint 10k-cap-then-truncate pattern is the public reference. 6) Per-key TTL + sliding-window eviction at primitive granularity to satisfy GDPR Recital 47 differential-retention (fraud-flagged fingerprints retained longer, clean ones dropped sooner). 7) Triggers / 'fire when (visitor_id, asset_id) crosses threshold' — device-farm and proximity alerts are inherently event-driven, polling 50+ features per identify is wasteful for the async path. 8) Secondary-index style queries like 'top-k visitor_ids by 24h linked_id n_unique' for the SOC analyst surface inside the vendor. 9) GDPR / CCPA right-to-erasure tooling — bulk delete by visitor_id or by linked_id, audit-logged, to handle data-subject requests. 10) PII / hashing story documented end-to-end: SHA-256 of IP + salt, no raw email in state, retention policy per primitive. 11) Cold-start strategy + WAL replay benchmarks at 50–200 GB state — a node restart during an active device-farm event cannot become an outage. 12) Per-region active-active or read-replica replication so a Frankfurt / Singapore / Virginia data-residency architecture is achievable. 13) A documented integration pattern with Kafka / Kinesis upstream of beava for the slow-path (training, analytics) while beava owns the hot path. 14) Benchmarks at production cardinality (10^8 keys, 5 primitives each) with p99 read latency curves — without this, the vendor's platform team cannot capacity-plan.
risk_and_non_goals.trigger_action_required: Yes — strongly. Device-intel vendors expose 'send a webhook when visitor X exceeds threshold' to their own customers, and re-implementing that on top of polling 50+ features per identify is wasteful. The async paths (proximity-cluster alerting, device-farm detection, cross-tenant abuse SOC alerts) all want 'fire when (visitor_id × asset_id_hash).count crosses N in 24h' as a primitive. This is one of the top-3 gaps for adoption in this domain alongside sharding and multi-tenancy.
